National context attached to this record: one LGBTIQ+ person was killed every 32 hours in 2025, a 63% increase over 2024 (270 vs 164 killings); 18% of the 164 homicides in 2024 were trans women; the government ombudsman counted at least 25 trans women murdered Jan–Sep 2025.

Nationally the article reports 13 trans people killed by hate in the first quarter of 2025, and cites earlier killings of gay men and the stabbing death of a trans rough-sleeper. It contains no finding specific to this department; for this record its value is national context: lethal anti-trans violence can occur in daylight, filmed, with the perpetrator unarrested.

No finding specific to this department appears; the violence-and-displacement pattern by armed actors is the claim this record relies on.

rewrites.blindSummary:
This department carries no local statute aimed at trans people and no department-level incident entry in the audited record; what a trans visitor stands under is the country's national pattern. That pattern is violent and largely unpunished: armed groups circulated "social cleansing" flyers naming trans women as targets in 2024, at least 41 trans women were killed nationally in 2023 and 13 more in the first quarter of 2025, and of 155 criminal investigations into LGBTQ killings only 3 reached a verdict last year — roughly 2% against a 9% overall homicide-conviction rate.

The government response to this violence is episodic rather than structural: the audited record shows a presidential order to investigate after a viral April 2025 murder of a trans woman in another department, vigils, and nothing resembling standing local protection machinery. Outside the largest cities the national figures are the operative risk for a visitor here.
